evidence: Parent plan: 'comment truncation takes the vendor's comment-limit/truncation contract. Cloud constructs those contract objects in adapters/jira/ from its pinned adf.py / comment_limits.py'
J2 Approach: '_sanitize_comment receives the vendor comment-limit contract' — no child defines what this contract is

findings.finding: No child formally defines or claims ownership of the comment-truncation contract that the parameterized `_sanitize_comment` in `jira_family/` requires. The parent plan states `_sanitize_comment` takes 'the vendor's comment-limit/truncation contract' as an injected dependency, analogous to `RichTextCodec` for description. J3 defines `RichTextCodec` but says nothing about comment truncation. No child names this contract, its Protocol shape, or which story owns it.
findings.location: child aac8-b283-22c1-4e66: J3 — Scope; child 62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743: J2 — Approach (parameterized _sanitize_comment)
scenarios: Implementer of J2 must decide on the fly what the comment-truncation contract's interface is (a Callable, a Protocol with truncate+max_chars, etc.) — different implementers of J6 (DC) and Cloud choose incompatible shapes
The contract ends up as an ad-hoc callable in J2 that J3 doesn't widen to a full Protocol, leaving DC (J6) without a well-specified interface for its plain-text comment limit
findings.suggested_fix: Extend J3's scope to include a `CommentLimitCodec` (or `CommentTruncator`) Protocol alongside `RichTextCodec`, with `CloudCommentCodec` (wrapping `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body`) in `adapters/jira/` and `PlainTextCommentCodec` in `jira_family/`, following the same pattern as AdfCodec vs WikiTextCodec.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Declare how the DC transport handles third-party library (pycontribs/jira / requests / urllib3) auth-header exposure at DEBUG log level: either suppress Authorization headers in the HTTP adapter's logging, document that operators must not enable DEBUG-level HTTP logging in production, or add a note to the operator docs naming this risk — so the security posture is complete, not just rebar's own code path.
evidence: 'The DC transport never logs the token' — plan Step 7, scoped to rebar's own code
'DC transport builds on the maintained pycontribs/jira library' — Step 4
pycontribs/jira uses requests under the hood; requests/urllib3 will emit Authorization headers at DEBUG log level when logging is enabled
Plan is silent on suppressing or sanitizing third-party HTTP library log output on the boundary-crossing path
findings.finding: The plan constrains rebar's own transport code to never log the PAT, but does not address whether `pycontribs/jira`'s underlying HTTP-level debug logging (via `requests`/`urllib3` at DEBUG verbosity) could expose the `Authorization: Bearer <PAT>` header in log output. If an operator enables DEBUG-level logging for troubleshooting, the third-party library may emit full request headers, leaking the PAT to log sinks.
findings.location: Step 4 / Step 7 — 'The DC transport never logs the token' constraint; `adapters/jira_datacenter/` transport implementation
scenarios: An operator enables DEBUG logging to diagnose a Jira connectivity issue; requests/urllib3 emits the full HTTP request including `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the PAT appears in operator log files or a centralized log aggregator.
A CI pipeline that runs the J5 live-harness tests enables verbose logging; the PAT used in the test environment leaks into the CI log artifact.
findings.suggested_fix: In the DC transport initialization, install a `logging.Filter` on the `urllib3.connectionpool` / `requests` loggers that redacts `Authorization` header values, or document in the operator guide that `PYTHONWARNINGS` / log-level guidance should exclude `urllib3` DEBUG output when a PAT is in use. Reference this in the AC for Step 7's security posture.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit rollback / back-out plan for the Cloud extraction: specify which commits or story branch to revert, or describe the feature-flag / dark-launch strategy that lets the old Cloud code path be restored without a full roll-forward.
evidence: 'Extend the existing held-out characterization tests…to pin the current outputs of every unit about to move, so any behavior change during extraction fails a pinned oracle.'
No 'revert by X' or 'back out by Y' instruction exists anywhere in the plan for the post-merge / post-deployment failure case.
Rubric: 'The remedy is an explicit rollback/back-out plan or expand-contract — acknowledgement alone is insufficient.'
findings.finding: The plan describes an expand-contract sequencing (freeze oracles before extracting) to prevent accidental Cloud breakage, but provides no explicit rollback or back-out plan if the extraction causes a behavioral regression that slips past the oracles into a deployed environment. The rubric requires an explicit rollback/back-out mechanism, not just detection.
findings.location: Approach §2 ('Freeze Cloud first') and AC line: 'characterization oracles pinning every unit…were committed before the extraction change was pushed'
scenarios: An extraction lands and passes all oracles in CI, but a subtle behavioral difference appears against a real Cloud Jira deployment (e.g., an oracle was written against a mock, not a real endpoint). The team has no documented recovery path.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Rollback' subsection to the Approach: 'If post-extraction Cloud behaviour diverges in production, revert the extraction commit (the oracle freeze commit is safe to retain). The Cloud adapter's old code paths are preserved in git history at <story-branch tip> for cherry-pick. No data-store migrations are involved, so revert is safe at any point before the DC story lands.' Also note this explicitly in the J2 story that lands the extraction.

No guard or note on what the schema validator returns between J6 and J7 if a user sets `reconciler.backend = "jira-datacenter"`.
findings.finding: The plan deliberately splits `_config_schema.py` changes between J6 (DC connection settings: `base_url`, `allow_insecure`, `ca_bundle`, `resolved_statuses`) and J7 (widening `reconciler.backend` to accept `"jira-datacenter"`). Between J6 and J7, the schema accepts DC connection keys but the `backend` selector does not yet accept `"jira-datacenter"`, creating a transient state where a user who sets those keys will get either a silent no-op or a validation error with no actionable message. This transient incompatibility is not acknowledged or guarded.
findings.location: Scope section: '`src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — widen `reconciler.backend` (owned by J7), add the TLS/`allow_insecure` validator and the `ca_bundle` + `resolved_statuses` keys (owned by J6). Split deliberately.'
scenarios: A developer integrates a partially-landed stack (J6 merged, J7 pending) and tests with `reconciler.backend = "jira-datacenter"` — they get a confusing schema rejection or silent failure with no explanation.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm how `outbound_fields.py`'s standalone-load bootstrap (the `spec_from_file_location` path used in tests) will resolve a `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import ...` import — either extend the bootstrap to seed `jira_family` into `sys.modules` before exec, or restructure the import so the standalone path remains loadable without package context (e.g. a lazy import inside the functions that use the map, or having the bootstrap in each test that loads it standalone also seed `jira_family`).
evidence: outbound_fields.py:33–49 bootstraps only `rebar_reconciler._loader` for the standalone path; no mechanism exists to also bootstrap `rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family` in that context

`_loader.py:56`: `path = _PACKAGE_DIR / filename` — resolves from `rebar_reconciler/` root; a `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import ...` in the exec'd module will fail without package context
outbound_fields.py comment: 'the differ may be spec-loaded by file path in tests, where `from . import` does not resolve'
findings.finding: The plan dependency-inverts `outbound_fields.py` (a pinned, location-fixed module that is also loaded standalone via `spec_from_file_location` in tests) so that it imports from `adapters/jira_family/`. However, `outbound_fields.py`'s standalone-load bootstrap (lines 33–49) only manually bootstraps `rebar_reconciler._loader`; it does not — and cannot automatically — make `rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family` resolvable in the no-package-context exec path. Once the dict-literal imports from `jira_family/` are added, any test that loads `outbound_fields` via `spec_from_file_location` without a full package context will raise `ModuleNotFoundError` on the new import. The plan states 'Editing a pinned module's contents is safe' but does not address this specific failure mode for the standalone-load test path, which is load-bearing for the existing characterization and differ test suites.
findings.location: Approach §2 — 'Stays put (path-wise)' / 'the pinned module is parameterized by the `jira_family` contracts (it imports *from* `jira_family/`)'
scenarios: Any existing test that injects `outbound_fields` via `spec_from_file_location` (the standalone-load path) breaks with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family'` once the dict imports are added

The J1 characterization-test step (which must pass before extraction) would surface this failure, but only if the test infrastructure doesn't happen to have already imported the package normally — a subtly environment-dependent failure
findings.suggested_fix: Add a parallel bootstrap block in `outbound_fields.py`'s standalone-load preamble (mirroring the existing `_loader` bootstrap) that seeds `rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family` via `spec_from_file_location` before the module-level `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import ...` executes; or move the cross-package import inside a function body so the module-level standalone exec never triggers it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Amend the harness docker command (J5 story) to bind only to loopback — `docker run -dit -p 127.0.0.1:2990:2990 pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` — so the no-auth/loopback-only rationale is structurally enforced rather than assumed.
evidence: Plan quotes: `docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` and `reachable at http://localhost:2990/jira`
T10(b2): the plan's implicit loopback-only no-auth rationale is not enforced by the command given — `-p 2990:2990` binds 0.0.0.0:2990, not 127.0.0.1:2990

findings.finding: The Docker command `docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` binds port 2990 to all network interfaces (0.0.0.0) by default, not to loopback only. The plan's no-auth rationale for the stood-up Jira web UI rests on it being loopback-only, but the command as written exposes the plain-HTTP Jira instance (with its default credentials) to any machine that can reach the CI runner or developer host, undermining that rationale. Human/admin authentication to the Jira web UI is not separately specified.
findings.location: Step 5 — 'Verify against a real Jira' / docker run command; AC: operator-attested reconcile bullet
scenarios: A shared GitHub Actions runner or corporate CI host exposes the ephemeral Jira UI to other jobs or network peers during the test run, with default credentials over plain HTTP.
A developer running the harness locally on a machine with open firewall rules inadvertently exposes the test Jira to the local network.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `-p 2990:2990` with `-p 127.0.0.1:2990:2990` in the J5 harness spec and in any CI workflow step that invokes it. Update the plan text to say 'bound to loopback' rather than 'reachable at localhost:2990' so future readers cannot inadvertently drop the loopback pin.

scenarios: Implementer creates adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py with Protocol, WikiTextCodec, AND AdfCodec, importing adf.py — the import-contract AST test immediately fails CI
Implementer creates adapters/jira/adf_codec.py for AdfCodec but this file is not listed in J3's scope or file_impact, so a reviewer has no baseline to check against
findings.suggested_fix: Add to J3 Scope: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py` (new) — `AdfCodec` implementation wrapping `adf.py`; delegates to `fit_text_to_adf_limit`, satisfies `RichTextCodec` Protocol. Add to J3 AC: a line confirming `AdfCodec` lives in `adapters/jira/`, not `jira_family/`, verified by grep.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] J7 Acceptance Criteria includes: '`make test` passes including J1's characterization assertions unmodified — verified by `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py` green on the J7 branch.'
evidence: Epic AC6: 'the full oracle set passes against the post-extraction Cloud adapter'
J7 AC1: 'test_backend_contract.py's fixture includes jira-datacenter and the suite passes with no assertion weakened' — this is the contract suite, not the characterization suite
J1 pins exact-value oracles in test_backend_characterization.py; J2 AC1 requires they pass after J2; J3 AC2 and J4 AC5 require J1's pins pass after J3/J4 — but J7 has no such AC

J7 is the final assembly story that composes WikiTextCodec, NameIdentity, and the DC transport; if Cloud's backend.py is accidentally touched during this assembly, J1's pins would fail but no J7 AC names this check
findings.finding: J7's acceptance criteria do not include an explicit re-run gate for J1's characterization suite after the full assembly lands. Epic AC6 requires 'the full oracle set passes against the post-extraction Cloud adapter', but J7 (the last story touching the shared layer before J8) only asserts that `test_backend_contract.py` passes — a different suite. J1's characterization assertions could silently be broken by J7's wiring without any named AC in J7 catching it.
findings.location: child b4e3-1de0-3188-40a1: J7 — Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: A J7 implementer accidentally changes Cloud backend construction while wiring the DC backend factory — J1's characterization tests fail but no J7 AC names them as required to pass, so a reviewer may not notice
findings.suggested_fix: Add to J7 AC: '`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py` passes with no assertion modified — confirming Cloud behavior is unchanged by J7's assembly wiring.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] J3 Approach text removes the 'Either landing order works' clause and states instead: 'J2 must be merged first (it creates jira_family/ and the shared mapper); this story then widens J2's placeholder fit function to the full RichTextCodec.'
evidence: J3 Approach: 'if J2 lands first with a minimal Callable[[str], str] fit function as a placeholder, this story widens that placeholder to the full RichTextCodec and re-points the sanitizer at it. Either landing order works'
J2 ticket deps: J2 blocks J3 (link_uuid 490584a4-eb4b-4691-9217-89f631f0b41d) — J2 must be merged before J3 can be pushed for review
J3 approach text states 'Either landing order works' which directly contradicts the blocks relationship
findings.finding: J3's approach says 'if J2 lands first with a minimal `Callable[[str], str]` fit function as a placeholder, this story widens that placeholder to the full `RichTextCodec`' — implying J2 and J3 can land in either order — yet the formal dependency graph records J2 as blocking J3, making J3 first an error. This contradicts the dependency relationship and may mislead an implementer into attempting to merge J3 before J2.
findings.location: child aac8-b283-22c1-4e66: J3 — Approach (second paragraph)
scenarios: An implementer reads J3's 'either landing order works' and begins J3 before J2 is merged, creating a branch that cannot be reviewed because its blocker is not closed
A reviewer of J3 sees 'either order works' and does not check whether J2's Gerrit change is merged, accepting J3 prematurely
findings.suggested_fix: Delete 'Either landing order works; what must not happen is jira_family/ importing the pinned adapters/jira/adf.py directly.' and replace with 'J2 is a prerequisite; this story widens J2's placeholder to the full RichTextCodec once J2 is merged.'

findings.finding: The `resolved_statuses` config key is a named deliverable in the plan body (Approach Step 2 describes it as operator-configured via `reconciler.resolved_statuses`, with a default and a config schema entry; Scope attributes it to J6 in `_config_schema.py`) but no AC verifies its existence, default behavior, or configurability. An implementer could omit it and the epic would still close against all stated criteria.
findings.location: Approach Step 2 (resolved_statuses description); Scope (`_config_schema.py` — owned by J6); Acceptance Criteria (no matching criterion)
findings.suggested_fix: Add: '`reconciler.resolved_statuses` is a validated config key (list of strings, optional); when unset it defaults to `["Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"]`; `classify_probe_response` in `jira_family/` receives the operator-configured set at DC construction time, verified by a unit test with a non-default status list.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the REST endpoint (or UI automation step) used to mint a PAT on the pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1 instance (e.g., `POST /rest/pat/1.0/tokens` with admin credentials) and confirm it is reachable on 8.17.1 — add this to J5's scope or the harness conftest spec.
evidence: J5 AC: 'a smoke test creates and reads back an issue via REST v2, and a PAT-authenticated request succeeds'
J5 testing section: 'auth path: a Personal Access Token minted on the 8.17.1 instance authenticates a request via Authorization: Bearer, proving the DC auth mode'
Plan body: 'Jira 8.17.1 is ≥ 8.14, the release that introduced Personal Access Tokens, so PAT bearer auth is exercised for real'
Neither the epic plan nor J5 names the REST endpoint (e.g., POST /rest/pat/1.0/tokens) or UI step used to create the PAT in the containerized instance
Evidence class: Unverified — the PAT-creation endpoint for Jira DC 8.17.1 is not confirmed in the plan text
findings.finding: The J5 child story's 'auth path' test requires minting a Personal Access Token on the 8.17.1 Dockerized Jira instance to prove Bearer auth, but neither the epic plan nor J5 names the REST endpoint or UI automation step used to create that PAT programmatically. Jira Server/DC does not expose PAT creation via a stable public REST endpoint before version 8.14, and the creation path (user profile UI, or `POST /rest/pat/1.0/tokens`) must be confirmed for 8.17.1.
findings.location: Approach §5 / J5 story — 'auth path: a Personal Access Token minted on the 8.17.1 instance authenticates a request via Authorization: Bearer'
scenarios: The J5 conftest needs to programmatically create a PAT for CI automation; if the endpoint is wrong or requires a UI step not scriptable via REST, the harness cannot run unattended in CI
The pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1 container may not expose PAT creation at the expected endpoint, causing the 'auth path' test to fail with a 404 and no clear diagnostic
findings.suggested_fix: In J5's conftest spec, add: the PAT is created via `POST http://localhost:2990/jira/rest/pat/1.0/tokens` with `Authorization: Basic <admin:admin base64>` and body `{"name": "ci-pat", "expirationDuration": 1}`; verify this endpoint returns 201 on 8.17.1 before committing the harness. If unavailable, fall back to the `/rest/api/2/mypermissions`-verified admin token pattern.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify whether `reconciler.resolved_statuses` is a DC-only config key (gated in the schema on `reconciler.backend = "jira-datacenter"`) or a global key that Cloud silently ignores, and make the Approach and Scope sections consistent on this point.
evidence: 'Cloud continues to pass its own frozenset, so Cloud is not made configurable by this change'
'src/rebar/_config_schema.py — … add the TLS/allow_insecure validator and the ca_bundle + resolved_statuses keys (owned by J6)'
findings.finding: The Approach (§2) states 'Cloud continues to pass its own frozenset, so Cloud is not made configurable by this change' for `resolved_statuses`, yet the Scope section adds `reconciler.resolved_statuses` as a new key in the global `_config_schema.py` (not a DC-only schema block). This creates a cross-section tension: the Approach promises Cloud is unaffected by the configurability, but placing the key at the top-level `reconciler` schema means Cloud operators can set it (or get confusing validation errors if they typo it), which contradicts the 'Cloud is not made configurable' claim.
findings.location: Approach §2 ('Cloud continues to pass its own frozenset, so Cloud is not made configurable by this change'); Scope ('src/rebar/_config_schema.py … add the … resolved_statuses keys (owned by J6)')
scenarios: A Cloud user sets `reconciler.resolved_statuses` expecting it to work, finds it silently ignored; or the schema rejects it as an unknown key for Cloud — either contradicts the Approach's intent or requires undescribed backend-conditional schema validation logic.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the `ca_bundle` config key's value type (absolute file path to a PEM bundle), its precedence relative to `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, and how the DC transport passes it to the underlying `pycontribs/jira` client.
evidence: 'an operator with an internal CA points rebar at their CA bundle (a `ca_bundle` config key / the standard `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` env var honoured by the underlying client)'
The AC for J6 is only indirectly referenced; the epic-level operator-docs AC says 'how to point rebar at an internal CA bundle' without pinning which mechanism to document.
No type, validation rule, or precedence order is stated for `ca_bundle`.
findings.finding: The `ca_bundle` config key semantics are underspecified: the plan names the key and the `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` env var in the same sentence ('a `ca_bundle` config key / the standard `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` env var honoured by the underlying client') but does not state whether they are independent mechanisms, which takes precedence, or what the key's value type is (file path string? directory? boolean to use system store?).
findings.location: Approach §7 ('Certificate verification stays ON') and Scope bullet 'add the TLS/`allow_insecure` validator and the `ca_bundle` + `resolved_statuses` keys (**owned by J6**)'
scenarios: J6's implementer adds `ca_bundle` as a file-path string but the underlying `pycontribs/jira` client passes it differently than `requests` expects, breaking cert verification silently.
An operator sets both `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` and `ca_bundle`; undefined precedence causes confusing behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: State: '`ca_bundle` is a string config key holding an absolute path to a PEM-format CA bundle; it maps to the `options={"verify": <path>}` argument of `JIRA()`; if both `ca_bundle` and `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` are set, `ca_bundle` takes precedence.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Merge AC2 and AC7 into a single criterion that specifies both the fixture mechanism and the 'not only adapter-local tests' constraint, or clearly distinguish them by stating what AC7 verifies that AC2 does not (e.g., that DC-specific adapter tests do not *substitute* for the contract suite).
evidence: AC2: 'test_backend_contract.py's backend fixture includes jira-datacenter and the suite passes for it'
AC7: 'JiraDataCenterBackend is exercised by the backend-agnostic contract suite, not only by adapter-local tests'
findings.finding: AC2 ('test_backend_contract.py's backend fixture includes jira-datacenter and the suite passes for it') and AC7 ('JiraDataCenterBackend is exercised by the backend-agnostic contract suite, not only by adapter-local tests') are near-duplicate criteria targeting the same verification goal — running the shared contract suite against the DC backend. The distinction (fixture configuration vs. suite-scope guarantee) is real but thin; in practice both criteria reduce to 'the contract suite passes for jira-datacenter,' meaning a reviewer could satisfy one and claim both satisfied.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC2 and AC7
scenarios: A reviewer marks both AC2 and AC7 green by checking one CI run; the near-duplication wastes review bandwidth and inflates the criterion count without adding verification coverage.
findings.suggested_fix: Merge into: 'The `test_backend_contract.py` backend fixture includes `jira-datacenter`, the full backend-agnostic contract suite passes for it, and the DC adapter has no adapter-local tests that substitute for (rather than supplement) that suite.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to the required ADR content (or operator docs) an explicit description of how `RemoteRef.instance` differentiates Cloud vs DC deployments in a shared store: what value to set, how the engine reads it for routing, and a worked example of a dual-instance config.
evidence: 'DC and Cloud share the single `jira` creation channel, `jira-` local-id prefix, and `jira_key` binding; deployments are disambiguated by the `RemoteRef.instance` field that ADR 0035 §(d) already defines for exactly this.'
No AC line, operator-doc requirement, or ADR amendment item covers how an operator sets or interprets `RemoteRef.instance` in a dual-backend scenario.
The new ADR's required contents are listed as 'the Jira-family sub-seam, the shared `jira` provenance identity, and the DC EOL horizon' — `instance`-based routing is not listed.
findings.finding: The plan invokes `RemoteRef.instance` as the disambiguation mechanism for operators running both a Cloud and a DC Jira instance against the same rebar store, but provides no operator-facing documentation on how to configure `instance`, what values are valid, or how the engine routes to the correct backend based on it. An operator trying to set up a dual-instance deployment has no documented path.
findings.location: Provenance decision section: 'deployments are disambiguated by the `RemoteRef.instance` field that ADR 0035 §(d) already defines for exactly this.'
scenarios: A federal client (CMS) runs both a legacy Cloud project and a new DC project simultaneously; the operator has no doc on how to configure `instance` to route bindings correctly, leading to mis-routing or duplicate-key collisions.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the ADR's required content list to: '…the Jira-family sub-seam, the shared `jira` provenance identity, the DC EOL horizon, **and how `RemoteRef.instance` is set and used to route Cloud-vs-DC bindings in a dual-deployment scenario**.' Add a corresponding AC line or operator-doc requirement.
